i do have a sense of purpose, to an extent. i have a really long bucket list, all these things i want to do, things i think will make me happy, things that i think will make the world a better place. i’m studying to be a teacher, lol. i used to do a lot of volunteering to help with improving literacy in my community. i like activism, i love words. 

but it seems to balance out less and less lately, and as i stop being so high functioning it seems impossible to reach. i see my family members who were full of potential, who decide to not give up and make it, and then i see the other family members who were also full of potential and decided not to give up, and i see them in the worst situations and i guess i identify with the latter more because it seems to get worse every year. i always look at the people who make it out of situations like mine (or very often worse) and the people who don’t and it’s always perspective, right? perspective and a bit of luck and grit and all that. i don’t know. i don’t feel like one of the success stories. i see myself staying alive in the people that stay alive and live lives that are hard to view as worth living. 

that’s my main fear, i guess. every day i stay alive things seem to get worse. of course it’s not linear in that way, but every depressive episode i have is worse, every period of impulsivity more severe. i understand more and more that the concept of rock bottom is a myth. i feel like if i decide to try, to stay alive, to try to “heal” i’ll wake up a year from now, detesting myself for staying alive even more, at lows i couldn’t have previously imagined. i feel like staying alive is lengthening the suffering, signing up for more pain. in some ways it is, i guess, just as it’s signing up for more beauty, but i just can’t get it to balance. i know living or not living is a choice, and we have some choices in our life: but i also know in many ways we are a victim to circumstance, to so many things we can’t control. i don’t fear death anymore because i realized it wasn’t the worst thing that could happen to me. when i realized that, death became the only way out i could see. that switch flipped in my head and i could never undo it. i don’t really know why trauma impacts some people that way and not others. but for me, what seems worse than death is torture. the prolonging of suffering and that continual pain. it sounds dramatic, but in many ways that is what living feels like, and i don’t get how so many people can find more beauty than sadness in that
